## Purpose and Runtime Boundary
Chat2API is a cross-platform Electron desktop application that manages AI-provider web-session credentials and exposes them through a local OpenAI-compatible Koa proxy. The Electron main process owns credentials, persistent state, proxy lifecycle, logs, updates, and native UI; the React renderer is a management console. Main entry: `src/main/index.ts`; renderer entry: `src/renderer/src/main.tsx`; privileged bridge: `src/preload/index.ts`.

## Desktop Application Shell
The main process initializes windows, IPC, tray behavior, logging, and optional updates. Renderer-originated operations cross Electron IPC rather than directly accessing filesystem, credentials, or proxy internals. Native lifecycle/UI boundaries are concentrated in `src/main/window/manager.ts`, `src/main/tray/TrayManager.ts`, and `src/main/ipc/handlers.ts`. Update checking/install flow is handled by `src/main/updater/UpdaterManager.ts`.

## Persistence, Credentials, and Observability
Local application state is managed through a store layer for configuration, providers, and accounts; README identifies storage under `~/.chat2api/`, with account credentials encrypted. Request and app logs are separate subsystems, with sanitization before request-log persistence. Key paths: `src/main/store/store.ts`, `src/main/store/accounts.ts`, `src/main/requestLogs/manager.ts`, `src/main/requestLogs/sanitizer.ts`, `src/main/appLogs/manager.ts`.

## Provider and Authentication Domain
Built-in provider definitions establish supported models/account shapes, while custom-provider support extends this boundary. OAuth and in-app login adapters obtain or extract provider tokens/cookies; provider-specific web APIs are not exposed to the renderer directly. Main extension points are `src/main/providers/builtin/index.ts`, `src/main/providers/custom.ts`, `src/main/oauth/manager.ts`, and `src/main/oauth/adapters/index.ts`. Implemented adapters cover DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, Mimo, MiniMax, Perplexity, Qwen variants, and Z.ai.

## Local Proxy Request Pipeline
The proxy server accepts OpenAI-style chat/completions and model requests, optionally authenticates management calls, resolves model/account routing, then forwards to provider-specific adapters. Its principal HTTP boundary is `src/main/proxy/server.ts`; public routes are `src/main/proxy/routes/chat.ts`, `src/main/proxy/routes/completions.ts`, and `src/main/proxy/routes/models.ts`. Dispatch and provider transport translation live in `src/main/proxy/forwarder.ts` and `src/main/proxy/adapters/index.ts`, including provider-specific streaming adapters.

## Routing, Sessions, Prompting, and Context
Before forwarding, the proxy maps requested model names, chooses among eligible accounts according to configured load balancing, and maintains sessions/context. Prompt generation and injection adapt OpenAI/client requests to provider expectations, including client-specific prompt adapters. Core paths: `src/main/proxy/modelMapper.ts`, `src/main/proxy/loadbalancer.ts`, `src/main/proxy/sessionManager.ts`, `src/main/proxy/services/contextManagementService.ts`, and `src/main/proxy/adapters/prompt/PromptAdapterRegistry.ts`.

## Tool Calling and Management Surface
Universal tool calling is a distinct translation pipeline: it selects a provider/client protocol plan, injects tool instructions, parses provider stream output, and emits compatible tool-call responses. The central engine and protocol boundary are `src/main/proxy/toolCalling/ToolCallingEngine.ts`, `src/main/proxy/toolCalling/runtimePlan.ts`, and `src/main/proxy/toolCalling/protocols/index.ts`. Separately, authenticated management HTTP endpoints expose accounts, keys, configuration, mappings, sessions, proxy state, and tool-calling settings through `src/main/proxy/routes/management/index.ts`.

## Renderer Management Console
The React/Zustand renderer administers providers/accounts, proxy settings, models, API keys, sessions, logs, and dashboard telemetry through preload IPC. Application composition begins in `src/renderer/src/App.tsx`; state stores include `src/renderer/src/stores/proxyStore.ts` and `src/renderer/src/stores/providersStore.ts`; major operational pages include `src/renderer/src/pages/ProxySettings.tsx`, `src/renderer/src/pages/Providers.tsx`, and `src/renderer/src/pages/Logs.tsx`.
